messages:
Ava (oncall): getting paging alert — p99 for streaming sessions jumped to ~2.6s in us-west-2 after the canary push. noticed a lot of stalled streams (clients waiting on chunk).
Kai (sre): ack. seeing elevated queue length on the serving nodes for canary-model:v1.3. p95 also up ~350ms. how much traffic is on canary?
Jordan (ml): canary set to 10% traffic, 3 pods. rollout started ~10:12 UTC. I pushed a small attention optimization change and a different kv-cache config.
Ava (oncall): incident-bot — create incident, page pg-sre and pg-ml, sev:high, impact: degraded streaming for ~10% of traffic.
incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED — ID INC-2026-1123. Pager sent to pg-sre and pg-ml. Runbook: streaming stalls / p99 spike.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout detected for model canary-model:v1.3 -> traffic 10% (3 pods).
Kai (sre): root checks: host cpu/gpu utilization look normal, but goroutine queueing in inference proxy is high. network packet drops? net stats look fine. logs show repeated "write timeout" to downstream kv-cache on canary pods.
Jordan (ml): kv-cache was switched to aggressive prefix caching for v1.3; fallback to disabled caching is trivial. Ava / Kai, recommend routing canary to bypass cache or rollback canary if stalls continue.
Maya (product): any customer-facing impact? Support picked up 4 tickets re chat stalls for premium customers on us-west. We should notify CS and trigger status page if we can't fix in 10m.
Ava (oncall): quick mitigation plan: 1) reduce canary traffic to 0% (pause rollout), 2) disable kv-cache for canary pods, 3) monitor p95/p99 for 5m. If p99 does not drop, rollback canary. Kai, Jordan, take action.
Kai (sre): running command to reduce canary:
```
# scale down canary route to 0%
redwood-cli rollout update --model canary-model:v1.3 --traffic 0
```
Kai (sre): command submitted, deploy-bot acknowledged.
deploy-bot: roll update accepted. Routing change in progress.
Jordan (ml): disabling kv-cache on the canary containers now (hotfix config):
```
kubectl -n inference set env deployment/canary-model KV_CACHE_ENABLED=false
```
Jordan (ml): env update rolled, pods restarted.
Kai (sre): observability: p95 down to baseline in 45s, p99 trending down but some tail at ~1.8s still. queue length on proxy reduced ~70%.
Ava (oncall): good. keep monitoring. Jordan, please check whether the attention optimization interacts poorly with streaming chunking — we should validate in staging.
Jordan (ml): will repro locally. early hypothesis: optimization increases per-token compute for short contexts causing backend to block until chunk complete. also cache misses spike latency.
Maya (product): updating CS — send note: "We observed degraded streaming for a subset of users during canary rollout; mitigation in progress, will follow up."
Kai (sre): runbook next: if p99 remains >1.5s after 10m, fully rollback to v1.2:
```
# rollback canary entirely
redwood-cli rollout rollback --model canary-model --to-version v1.2
```
Ava (oncall): plan B ready. current p99 at 0.9s, p95 back to normal. switch to monitoring-only channel. I will start a short on-call handoff note for next shift with timeline and steps taken.
Ava (oncall): handoff note -> next oncall (Kai) at 18:00 UTC: incident id INC-2026-1123, mitigation: canary traffic reduced to 0%, kv-cache disabled on canary pods, observed p99 recovered to 0.9s. follow-up: run regression tests for attention change + streaming chunking, add canary circuit-breaker to disable cache automatically on errors.
Kai (sre): taking over monitoring. leaving this thread for documentation; will ack in 10m.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATED — status: mitigated, severity -> degraded -> monitoring.
Ava (oncall): closing sequence: file postmortem with timeline + customer impact. tagging eng-ml and eng-runtime owners.
Jordan (ml): will add repro logs and a minimal test to the canary pipeline.
Maya (product): prepping customer comms for affected accounts.
Kai (sre): mark this resolved if no regressions in 30m.
Ava (oncall): thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
